[0] everyday_reading (E): Folk meaning: in English, 'items 1 to 10' or 'up to n' includes the end point, and reading past the end of a list just gives 'nothing'. Java rule: the legal indices are 0..length-1, and any other index throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning a value.
[1] misconception (M) -> OutOfBoundsElementsAreNull: wrong rule: An out-of-bounds read returns null (or 0). Right rule: Reading or writing any index outside 0 to a.length - 1 throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException and returns no value.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> OutOfBoundsElementsAreNull: Points to LT: the bounds check runs at every access, at run time. Inconsistent application: the trace accepts an index of a.length on the last pass (or -1 on the first) but rejects it elsewhere, or reads 'some value' there. (here mixing in: "an out-of-bounds read returns null (it throws)")
[3] misconception (M) -> OffByOneBound: wrong rule: < vs <= and 0..n vs 0..n-1 are interchangeable. Right rule: for (i = 0; i < n; i++) runs n times with i going up to n - 1; with <= it runs n + 1 times and reaches i = n, which is out of bounds for an array of length n.

[0] names_the_element (N): Identity: the bounds of an array are its legal index range, 0 to length-1.
[1] states_the_rule (S): Declarative: an index less than 0 or greater than length-1 makes the program terminate with an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException; it is the programmer's responsibility to use legal indices.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): Sequencing: at each access the index expression is evaluated first and then compared with 0 and a.length. Only if it is in range is the element read or written; otherwise the exception is thrown before any element changes.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Result: a legal access yields the element. An illegal one yields no value; the program stops with ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException naming the bad index (old JVMs print ': 10', current ones 'Index 10 out of bounds for length 10').
[2] one_step_execution (OS): State transition: an out-of-bounds write changes no element, because the exception is raised before the store. Control leaves the statement, and main terminates unless the exception is caught.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): Every index value used in a[i] must satisfy 0 <= i <= a.length-1; the last element is a[a.length-1].
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): Because an out-of-bounds index stops the program, the loop test checks the bounds before the body uses the index (e.g. x > 0 && x < N-1 before a[x-1], a[x+1]).
[2] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Plan/role: run-time bounds checking makes an indexing mistake a visible error instead of silent memory corruption (buffer overflow).

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> OutOfBoundsElementsAreNull: Conservation: a loop bounded by i < a.length stays within bounds when the array size changes. Changing < to <= adds one pass that throws, and starting at 1 or ending at a.length-1 silently skips an element.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Applicability: check indices explicitly (or restrict the loop range) whenever an index is computed from data, a random number or a neighbour (i-1, i+1). A plain i < a.length traversal or an enhanced for loop needs no extra check.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Indices must be in 0..a.length-1. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: index >= a.length or < 0: i <= a.length, a[i+1] on the last pass, a[i-1] at i = 0, a[0] on an empty array, or the Sample program run with M > N (ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException)
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: A traversal must reach the last valid index a.length-1. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: the loop stops one short (i < a.length-1) or starts at 1, so the last or first element is never processed

Because an out-of-bounds index stops the program, the while test checks the bounds before the body uses the index.
An index outside 0 .. length-1 is not caught by the compiler; the access is checked when the program runs and stops it with ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
Valid indexes run from 0 to a.length - 1; any other index throws an exception when it is used.
